DC-2025-B260056.aiSummary: The bill would change how money from civil settlements for minor children is handled in the District of Columbia. It would require court approval for settlements worth $10,000 or more, and payment would go to a trustee and usually be placed in a blocked account until the child turns 18, with some court-approved options for other trusts or payment setups. A judge could still appoint a guardian of the child’s property if that is in the child’s best interest.

DC-2025-B260603.aiSummary: The bill would expand body camera release rules to cover cases where an MPD officer is present during a death or serious use of force by another law enforcement officer. It would also require MPD to include the names of other officers involved, when available, and to record details about other law enforcement officers at roll call. The department would have to share that roll call information with the Council committee chair on request, and some of it could be given to the public as summary data.

DC-2025-B260735.aiSummary: The law requires the District Department of Corrections to provide a free public education for certain people in its custody who have disabilities and are held in secure facilities. It applies to people age 18 through the end of their school eligibility under federal disability law and District law. The rule covers school years 2025-2026 and 2026-2027, and the act was signed and enacted on October 21, 2026.

DC-2025-B260427.aiSummary: The bill would require insurance licensees to keep a written cybersecurity program, do risk checks, and use safeguards to protect nonpublic information. It would also require prompt investigation of cybersecurity events and notice to the Department of Insurance, Securities, and Banking commissioner within 3 business days after one is found. The bill also makes a related change to the Freedom of Information Act.
